signals: Price is not the blocker — 'I don't mind paying that. I mean, if it's going to get me to that point at six months, I'm actually fine paying with that'
Wants refinement rather than rescue: 162 lb at 6'0", goal is 'more defined. Like, more athletic... not more, like, bodybuilder or anything'
Health-literate and self-quantifying: full blood panel, Oura Ring, already bought the equipment before the sales call

TENSION IN THIS ASSIGNMENT: he is not actually 'already fit' — he has no current training routine, is gym-averse ('one part I hate is what I don't like is actually going to the gym'), and says 'I've never been in a shape that I would like to be', which is neither an optimizer's good-to-great nor a rebuilder's former self

Also carries skeptical_bargain_hunter behaviour — asked for a new-customer discount and anchored to the company's own $200/month Primal University app — but has no cheap alternative that actually worked for him, so that avatar does not fit either. Proposed label for central clustering: 'the_structure_seeker' — capable, solvent, never had a plan, buying the schedule rather than the coaching

objections.raw_quote: I just, I want to make sure if you can, able to accept your money-wise so I can put it, not all upfront.
objections.rep_response: Offered a three-payment structure at $2,000 each with no interest, and noted a six-payment option would add roughly $1,200 overall. Prospect took the three-pay.

objections.raw_quote: There's no promotion for a new person, or any of that, or I don't know. Like don't you guys have any?
objections.rep_response: Held the price cleanly — 'So there is no, like, discount on the price itself. But we can structure the payment.' Also confirmed $6,000 covers everything and no equipment purchase is required beyond one kettlebell.

objections.raw_quote: I just wanted to kind of do some research before I commit to this, you know, 6K and all that stuff. That's all.
objections.rep_response: Asked whether anything was red-flagging him, asked what exactly was unclear ('Because I don't think I get it, to be honest'), asked him to read the room and whether he believed it could get him to his goals, and offered the try-it-to-know-it line. Then requested a $100 refundable deposit to hold the slot. Prospect declined and the rep conceded.

objections.raw_quote: But I still like to understand what other people are saying about this six-month program, other than what you guys said.
objections.rep_response: Pointed back to the testimonials already sent and shared a 54-year-old client's three-month before-and-after photos in the Zoom chat, then argued reviews cannot settle it: 'you can read all the reviews that you want, but eventually how actually you will know if you never actually tried it for yourself on your body.' No independent third-party proof was available.

objections.raw_quote: But I would, it's not that you, I have to pay on the first call. Usually first calls are introductions, explaining what it is and all that stuff.
objections.rep_response: Took it as a personal delivery failure — 'So it looks I haven't done my job properly if you don't have clarity until now' — and asked what was missing rather than addressing the expectation itself. Never acknowledged that the prospect had not been told this was a decision call.

tiers.note: three payments of $2,000, explicitly interest-free — the structure the prospect selected
six-payment option described as 'additional like 1,200 in overall'

offer.payment_plan_terms: 3 x $2,000 with no interest. A $100 refundable holding deposit was also proposed as a condition of taking time to decide, and declined.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent; the rep began the close ('let's get through the agreement and the payment') and the prospect diverted to asking for programme detail
The onboarding slot with Trevor for Tuesday the 28th at 3:15pm was booked and then explicitly unwound — 'you don't have to book anything for next week'
The $100 holding deposit was offered and not taken

Prospect ended on his own terms: 'once I'm good with this, I'll just text you and they're like, okay, I'm okay with moving forward. What's the next step?' Rep agreed: 'we'll schedule another call and meet and get you on board'
POSITIVE SIGNALS: strong stated intent throughout — 'I don't mind paying that', 'once I'm in, I'm in', 'I'm actually fine paying with that', and he had already bought a kettlebell set before the call
COUNTER-EVIDENCE against optimism: the reason for delay is unresolved third-party validation, which the company cannot supply, and he leaves controlling the next contact
outcome.next_step: Prospect will do independent research on the programme and text the rep when ready; a new call would then be booked to onboard. Rep left the ball entirely in the prospect's court with no scheduled follow-up date.

notable.note: A well-qualified, solvent, ready-to-buy prospect who had already purchased kettlebells and said outright he does not mind paying $6,000 — lost to the calendar, not to the price. Two structural problems caused it. First, an expectation mismatch: he believed a first call was an introduction, not a decision point, and said so explicitly. Second, the only proof available is first-party — he asked for independent reviews and there were none to give. The rep then attempted to convert the hesitation into a $100 refundable holding deposit, an instrument that appears nowhere in the offer, which reads as a commitment device rather than a payment. Also worth noting: the prospect had independently found the company's own $200/month Primal University app and had to be told it was a different product, the second time in this batch that the low-tier product has confused a $6,000 buyer.

quality.notes: Attribution is badly and frequently inverted in both directions. Long passages carry the wrong label outright: the entire injury-screening exchange from roughly 00:08:52 to 00:10:00 is collapsed under the prospect's 'ppatel' label but contains the rep's questions; the price reveal at 00:20:20 ('The full investment for that, in order to get you to your goals, is 6K') is labelled 'ppatel' but is unmistakably the rep; and the prospect's questions about discounts and tiers repeatedly appear under the rep's label. Roles were read from content throughout. Because of this the record contains no talk-ratio or first-speaker claims, only role-level facts.
